scope: Geometry and convergence diagnosis only; no product numerical code/default/quality changes; no new physical accuracy qualification.
conclusions: On the tested single straight plane, native cutting agrees with independent AMReX 2D EB geometry.
The common production small-cell agglomerator produces quality-admissible grids on which both native SIMPLE and OpenFOAM SIMPLE converge.
Raw extreme cells are rejected by the unchanged native quality gate; successful OpenFOAM residual stopping does not erase extended checkMesh failures.
On the original fine annulus both native SIMPLE and full-corrected OpenFOAM SIMPLE exhibit growing residuals, while native coupled solves the original discrete system.
Quality-guarded annulus merges do not eliminate the minimum neighbour area ratio. They do not isolate or exclude small cells as a cause. Unique causality remains unresolved.

controls.openfoamStopping: separate OpenFOAM residualControl p/U 1e-8, not the native normalization
controls.exactPressure: constant; remove volume-weighted mean for error

limits: Only single straight-plane reference geometry; not a curved/multiple-cut or adaptive-AMR generator qualification.
Shared native topology assembly and optional agglomerator mean these components are not independently cross-validated.
Across severity levels the wall intercept changes slightly; each within-level source comparison is matched, but severity is not a pure fixed-geometry area intervention.
Finite-volume spatial operators and stopping normalizations differ across solvers. No iteration-count or speed equivalence is asserted.
All twelve external matrix meshes passed standard checkMesh but failed at least one extended check. Errors and convergence are separately reported.
Original l5/l6/l7 have different polygon faceting; these observations are not a fixed-geometry convergence series.
First native-default-initialization matrix runs were excluded; only explicit-rest runs are in final matrix results.
